teaser: An iPhone app that only reads my newsroom: WebKit in the UK, a paid membership and a Mac to build it, one passkey test first, and someone else to maintain it.
core_idea: Frustration with phone browsers, plus the power to build, turns into a brief for a personal iPhone app that only reads the newsroom; in the UK it must be WebKit, passkeys and push need the paid membership, it must be built on a Mac, the vault's PRF passkey is the first test, and once it works even a power user wants someone else to maintain it.

quotes.text: Being able to compile a Linux kernel does not mean I want to compile Linux kernels
On an iPhone in the UK, the question answers itself.

figures.caption: A browser for one, sketched on an iPhone. It opens on the newsroom where it was left, with tabs in a strip that hides as you read, read and unread marked, the vault open, an inbox of what the agents sent, and reading workflows as runs of tabs. Underneath: a native Swift shell around WebKit, a small bridge to the page, an offline cache, and a push sender. The first step is a test: do passkeys with the PRF extension work inside the app.
